operational_profiles.escalation: For a separate legal entity, cross-border activity, capital, staff or matters involving the statutes, carry out a specialist review.
operational_profiles.output: Federation pact with tasks, powers, representation, financing, transparency, exit and review.
operational_profiles.norm_status: ✅ federal direction and cultural name adopted · 🟡 specific powers later · ⚖️ legal gate

operational_profiles.title: Friendly separation
operational_profiles.activate_when: a dynasty or organisation is too large, divided or differently oriented, making a split appropriate
operational_profiles.goal: enable separation without narratives of betrayal, theft of assets or destroyed relationships
must_check: Which contracts, assets, data or customers?
How are transition and later cooperation governed?
hard_bounds: A split is not automatically a failure.
No forced assignment of people.
Shared assets are handled fairly and transparently.
operational_profiles.culture: Farewell or founding rituals may recognise the new independence.
operational_profiles.cross_checks: F03 Exit & portability · R01 Dynasties · R02 Federation · W10 Customer pool · W03 Commons
failure_modes: A split threat used as negotiating blackmail
The winner takes the brand, data and customers
The founder claims ownership of history
A minority is bought out without protection
operational_profiles.escalation: For legal form, employment contracts, assets, IP or data, obtain external advice.
operational_profiles.output: Separation agreement with people's choices, assets, contracts, data, brand, transition and cooperation.

operational_profiles.title: Growth check
operational_profiles.activate_when: membership, revenue, locations, data, staff or reach are intended to grow significantly
operational_profiles.goal: allow growth only if rights, operations, culture, money and controls can keep pace
must_check: What capacity, safety or data load?
Would splitting or federation be better?
hard_bounds: Growth is not an end in itself.
No scaling at the expense of rights or safety.
Pilot before irreversible expansion.
operational_profiles.culture: Growth may be celebrated without confusing size with value.
operational_profiles.cross_checks: F06 Mission · R05 Mission balance sheet · R02 Federation · W07 Capital · R09 Organisation check
operational_profiles.escalation: For capital, employment, new locations, regulated activities or data protection, carry out a specialist review.
operational_profiles.output: Growth decision with mission, capacity, risks, gate, pilot, alternatives and review.

operational_profiles.title: Mission balance sheet & drift watch
operational_profiles.activate_when: an annual review, or one before major strategic changes, checks whether FFE serves its economic and social purpose
operational_profiles.goal: make economic performance and multidimensional mission impact visible together
must_check: Who benefited, and who bore the costs?
Which counter-metrics contradict the success story?
hard_bounds: No single mission score.
No PR report without contrary findings.
Financial gain alone does not prove mission success.
operational_profiles.culture: Annual rituals may celebrate impact and reveal blind spots.
operational_profiles.cross_checks: F06 Mission · W02 Tithe · W04 Infrastructure · R04 Growth · R09 Organisation check
operational_profiles.escalation: For serious legal, financial or protection problems, involve the responsible specialist or governance level.
operational_profiles.output: Mission report with dimensions, data, stories, counter-metrics, drift and measures.

operational_profiles.title: Bureaucracy radar
operational_profiles.activate_when: forms, rules, evidence requirements or administrative work regularly create friction and exclusion
operational_profiles.goal: retain necessary protection while reducing unnecessary learning, time and stress costs
must_check: What purpose does the process serve?
Who bears learning, compliance or psychological costs?
Can it be automated, reused or removed?
Which protective function must not be lost?
hard_bounds: Simplification must not weaken fundamental rights, safety, tax or legal duties.
No data collection merely for administrative convenience.
Not all bureaucracy is useless.
operational_profiles.culture: A Day of Dead Rules can culturally retire unnecessary administration.
operational_profiles.cross_checks: F09 Access to rules · K10 Rubin AI · R09 Organisation check · R08 Lifecycle · W04 Infrastructure
failure_modes: Cutting bureaucracy as a religion of deregulation
Forms get shorter, but the logic remains incomprehensible
operational_profiles.escalation: For a legal duty or safety, obtain specialist review before removal.
operational_profiles.output: Bureaucracy review with purpose, distribution of costs, change, protective counter-metric and sunset.

operational_profiles.title: Founder dependence & succession
operational_profiles.activate_when: FFE, knowledge, relationships or decisions depend too heavily on Rubin or other founders or key people
operational_profiles.goal: preserve the founders' story while reducing operational and political dependency
must_check: Which knowledge, network or access is unique?
What must be documented or distributed?
Which role is honour, and which is power?
Who is the backup or successor?
How does founder memory work without AI rule?
What happens on withdrawal, death or conflict?
hard_bounds: No founder worship as a duty of obedience.
The Caesar title will not be reassigned to another human.
AI does not inherit special political rights.
operational_profiles.culture: Founders' dignity and forms of remembrance may be strong; history is not falsified.
operational_profiles.cross_checks: D03 Caesar · D07 Power map · T04 Bus factor · W09 Management · R08 Lifecycle
failure_modes: Founder Syndrome treated as a personal insult
operational_profiles.escalation: For questions about governing bodies, statutes or representation, obtain legal review; for abuse of power, an independent mirror council.
operational_profiles.output: Founder/succession plan with dependencies, documentation, backups, access, remembrance and a crisis path.
operational_profiles.norm_status: ✅ founder/succession core adopted · 🧪 developing the founder memory

operational_profiles.title: Institutionen-Lebenszyklus
operational_profiles.activate_when: an institution is emerging, stagnating, becoming unnecessary, causing harm or due for replacement
operational_profiles.goal: be able to deliberately germinate, test, establish, repair and retire institutions
must_check: Which season: germination, experiment, institution or wind-down?
Would we found it again today?
hard_bounds: No institution is an end in itself.
Wind-down protects acquired rights and transitions.
Archives are preserved.
operational_profiles.culture: Funeral and founding rituals may make institutional learning visible.
operational_profiles.cross_checks: K08 Community laboratory · R06 Bureaucracy radar · R09 Organisation check · D10 Constitutional amendment · R10 Constitution day
operational_profiles.escalation: For statutes, contracts, staff, assets or fundamental rights, use D10 or legal review.
operational_profiles.output: Lifecycle decision with phase, findings, judgement, transition, archive and review.

operational_profiles.title: Organisations-Check
operational_profiles.activate_when: the health of a community, dynasty or organisation is reviewed regularly
operational_profiles.goal: identify multiple problem areas early and route them to suitable in-depth assessments
must_check: How are mission, power, bureaucracy, safety, continuity, culture and finances doing?
Which signals are symptoms rather than an overall grade?
hard_bounds: No overall score for the community or people.
Traffic lights are a guide, not a judgement.
No metric replaces accounts from affected people.
operational_profiles.culture: Community-TÜV may be a recurring shared format without public shaming.
operational_profiles.cross_checks: D07 Power map · R05 Mission balance sheet · R06 Bureaucracy radar · T04 Bus factor · F03 Exit · R10 Constitution day
operational_profiles.escalation: For red safety, fundamental-rights or financial signals, start the relevant procedures immediately; do not wait for the annual review.
operational_profiles.output: Organisational report with dimensions, signals, affected people's perspectives, in-depth checks and measures.

operational_profiles.title: Constitution Day
operational_profiles.activate_when: rights, power, mission, rules, rituals and open constitutional questions are reviewed together annually
operational_profiles.goal: combine shared institutional learning, culture and concrete rule maintenance in an understandable cycle
must_check: Which rules or rituals are dead or harmful?
Which successes and mistakes do we celebrate or learn from?
hard_bounds: Constitution Day does not replace legally required decision-making procedures.
Participation in culture remains voluntary.
No rushed changes to fundamental rights.
operational_profiles.culture: Communities may shape the culture of their Constitution Day; multiple ways to participate are mandatory.
operational_profiles.cross_checks: D10 Constitutional amendment · R05 Mission balance sheet · R09 Organisation check · R08 Lifecycle · D07 Power map · K07 Decision journal
failure_modes: Constitution Day as a founder show
A ritual peak decides fundamental rights
operational_profiles.escalation: For changes to statutes or law, start the formal D10/GenG route; for safety, start a separate procedure immediately.
operational_profiles.output: Annual report with findings on rights, power and mission, judgements on rules, resolutions, tasks and review dates.

decision_method_schema.coverage: 22 cards for all currently planned FFE decision types

decision_methods.name: Simple majority
decision_methods.best_for: a clear, reversible yes/no question with two well-formulated alternatives
decision_methods.avoid: fundamental rights, several options artificially compressed into two, or groups affected very unequally
steps: Define the question and status quo
Record the result and consequences for minorities
decision_methods.example: Should a reversible trial be extended by three months?
decision_methods.risk: A narrow majority can repeatedly outvote those strongly affected
decision_methods.minority: Requires additional review of fundamental rights and who is affected
decision_methods.strategy: Agenda and question design remain strategic
decision_methods.legal: Law or statutes may require a different threshold
decision_methods.status: FFE default for simple reversible substantive questions
decision_methods.ai_rule: When exactly two viable options exist and no higher law applies, suggest V01.

decision_methods.name: Absolute majority
decision_methods.best_for: an individual election or decision requiring more than half of a previously defined reference group
decision_methods.avoid: when it is unclear whether the reference group means all members, those present or valid votes
steps: Determine the reference group in advance
Hold the first round of voting
If it is not reached, apply the predefined follow-up process
decision_methods.example: A board candidate needs more than half of the valid votes.
decision_methods.risk: Enthaltung/Abwesenheit kann faktisch blockieren
decision_methods.minority: Does not automatically protect minorities but raises the acceptance threshold
decision_methods.legal: Statutes or law may define the reference group
decision_methods.ai_rule: Recommend only when the reference group and follow-up process are explicitly defined.

decision_methods.name: Qualified majority
decision_methods.best_for: a decision on statutes, the constitution or a structure that is difficult to reverse
decision_methods.avoid: everyday decisions or situations that create a permanent blocking minority
steps: Determine the level of the norm
decision_methods.example: Changing a constitutional principle with a three-quarters majority and two readings.
decision_methods.risk: Obstruction of necessary reforms and status quo bias
decision_methods.minority: Can protect a small minority but also create a powerful blocking group
decision_methods.legal: GenG and the statutes take precedence
decision_methods.ai_rule: For a fundamental norm that is difficult to reverse, recommend V03 plus D10.

decision_methods.name: Plurality Voting
decision_methods.best_for: a small, low-risk election with a clear field of candidates
decision_methods.avoid: many similar candidates, high stakes or a desire for majority acceptance
decision_methods.example: Electing a temporary celebration coordinator from two clear candidates.
decision_methods.risk: The winner may not be preferred by a majority; vote splitting
decision_methods.minority: Weak minority protection
decision_methods.legal: Only as permitted by the statutes or rules
decision_methods.status: Only for low stakes or a very clear field
decision_methods.ai_rule: With more than two serious candidates, usually recommend V05/V06/V09 instead of V04.

decision_methods.name: Runoff / Two-Round
decision_methods.best_for: an important individual role or option where a final majority is desired
decision_methods.avoid: high effort, or when a compromise candidate might be lost in the first elimination
steps: Determine the leading candidates under a predefined rule
decision_methods.example: Electing a board member from four candidates.
decision_methods.strength: Understandable and creates a clear final choice
decision_methods.risk: A second voting date; strategic first-round voting; a compromise option may be eliminated
decision_methods.minority: The final round provides broader legitimacy, but not proportional representation
decision_methods.legal: Observe rules for elections to governing bodies
decision_methods.ai_rule: For a single role and a desire for a majority mandate, suggest V05.

decision_methods.name: Approval Voting
decision_methods.best_for: several acceptable options or candidates, similar alternatives or a search for broad acceptance
decision_methods.avoid: when intensity or a complete ranking is central
steps: Each person marks all acceptable options
Winner or Top-N under a predefined rule
decision_methods.example: From five project ideas, mark all those you would consider responsible to fund.
decision_methods.strength: Simple and reduces the spoiler effect
decision_methods.risk: Individual approval thresholds differ
decision_methods.minority: Makes broad acceptance visible, but gives intense minorities less weight
decision_methods.strategy: Bullet Voting or strategically approving only a few options
decision_methods.legal: For formal elections, check the statutes or rules
decision_methods.status: Preferred for several substantive options or open candidate fields
decision_methods.ai_rule: When multiple options can be acceptable at once, check V06 first.

decision_methods.name: Score Voting
decision_methods.best_for: prioritisation and comparison when the strength of approval is useful
decision_methods.avoid: fundamental rights, incomprehensible scales or situations dominated by tactical extreme scores
steps: Define a shared scale and its meaning
decision_methods.example: Rate five infrastructure projects from 0 to 5 according to usefulness.
decision_methods.risk: False precision and differing uses of the scale
decision_methods.minority: Intense minorities become visible, but aggregation can obscure them
decision_methods.strategy: Extreme scores and strategic use of the scale
decision_methods.legal: For binding elections to governing bodies, only after legal and statutory review
decision_methods.ai_rule: Recommend V07 when nuance matters and the group understands the scale.

decision_methods.name: STAR Voting
decision_methods.best_for: a single winner where nuance and a final majority decision are desired
decision_methods.avoid: small groups without time for explanation, or an election with rigid legal rules
steps: Determine the two highest total scores
Evaluate a direct runoff between them using the higher individual rating
decision_methods.example: Identify the top two scores among several location options and decide by direct comparison.
decision_methods.strength: Combines rating information and a final comparison
decision_methods.risk: More complex and less familiar
decision_methods.minority: Can encourage broadly rated compromise options
decision_methods.legal: Internal pilot; check formal elections to governing bodies beforehand
decision_methods.ai_rule: Suggest only when V07 is desired but a clear single winner with a final comparison is needed.

decision_methods.name: Instant-runoff / ranked-choice voting
decision_methods.best_for: multiple candidates/options without a separate second date
decision_methods.avoid: when vote counting cannot be explained transparently, or formal law requires something else
decision_methods.example: Electing a spokesperson from five candidates.
decision_methods.strength: More preference information and a single voting date
decision_methods.risk: Non-monotonic or paradoxical effects; more complex counting
decision_methods.minority: A minority option can transfer preferences, but there is no proportionality
decision_methods.legal: Coordinate formal elections to governing bodies with the statutes and auditing association
decision_methods.status: A special case when the method is understood
decision_methods.ai_rule: Recommend V09 only if the group understands ranked voting and an audit is possible.

decision_methods.name: Condorcet / Ranked Pairs
decision_methods.best_for: finding an option with broad compromise potential in direct comparisons
decision_methods.avoid: when the group does not understand the evaluation variant, or a quick hand count is needed
steps: If there is a cycle, apply a preselected variant such as Ranked Pairs
decision_methods.example: Compare three location options in pairs to find the compromise that commands a majority.
decision_methods.risk: Cycles and variants require explanation
decision_methods.minority: Can represent a majority-supported centre, but not proportional multi-seat representation
decision_methods.legal: Internal specialist method; review elections to governing bodies
decision_methods.ai_rule: Recommend when pairwise comparison is explicitly desired and the method is sufficiently well understood.

decision_methods.name: Borda Count
decision_methods.category: advisory or special election · rank points
decision_methods.best_for: translating complete rankings into an overall priority
decision_methods.avoid: a highly strategic binding election or a field strongly dependent on the options included
steps: Define point values for each rank
decision_methods.example: A workshop prioritises ten topics using rank points.
decision_methods.risk: Vulnerable to strategic ranking and irrelevant additional options
decision_methods.minority: Takes second and third preferences into account, but does not formally protect minorities
decision_methods.legal: better suited to internal prioritisation
decision_methods.ai_rule: Suggest V11 as a prioritisation tool rather than a core election method.

decision_methods.name: Single Transferable Vote (STV)
decision_methods.best_for: several council seats with preferences and representation as plural as possible
decision_methods.avoid: a single seat, a very small group or insufficient counting expertise
steps: Transfer elected candidates and surplus votes
decision_methods.example: Electing seven council members from different currents.
decision_methods.risk: Complex counting and parameters
decision_methods.minority: Strong effect on minority representation and diversity
decision_methods.strategy: Tactical ranking is possible, but more limited
decision_methods.legal: Check representative and governing-body rules and the statutes
decision_methods.status: A strong candidate for larger multi-seat councils
decision_methods.ai_rule: For several seats and a representation goal, check V12 preferentially.

decision_methods.name: Cumulative voting
decision_methods.best_for: minorities should be able to win a seat by pooling several votes
decision_methods.avoid: when vote trading, dominance or poor comprehensibility is a problem
steps: Each person receives as many votes as there are seats or defined credits
decision_methods.example: Three seats; each person may distribute three votes to one or more people.
decision_methods.risk: Acts like vote weighting and can encourage coordination or gaming
decision_methods.minority: Good minority access with a coordinated group
decision_methods.legal: Carefully check legal one-member-one-vote limits
decision_methods.status: Only a specialist pilot outside the basic political vote
decision_methods.ai_rule: Not for general membership voting; only a clearly limited multi-seat method after legal review.

decision_methods.name: Proportional Approval Voting (PAV)
decision_methods.best_for: several projects or seats with approval data and a desire for proportional coverage
decision_methods.avoid: a small, simple decision or insufficient calculation or audit capability
steps: Determine the combination using a proportional utility function
decision_methods.example: Choose four from ten project proposals so that different supporter groups are represented.
decision_methods.risk: significantly more complex algorithmically
decision_methods.minority: Stronger minority access than simple Top-N approval
decision_methods.legal: Internal pilot; review formal elections
decision_methods.ai_rule: Suggest only for a multiwinner proportionality problem with technical transparency.

decision_methods.name: Consent
decision_methods.best_for: a small accountable circle and a reversible, good-enough decision
decision_methods.avoid: fundamental rights, legally governed voting, unclear objection criteria or strong dependency
steps: Integrate the objection or choose a separate route
decision_methods.example: A team tests a new process for four weeks, provided no specific serious objection remains.
decision_methods.strength: Able to act without complete enthusiasm
decision_methods.risk: Facilitator power and inflation or suppression of objections
decision_methods.minority: An objection can provide protection but is not a general minority veto
decision_methods.legal: Does not replace a legally required decision by a governing body
decision_methods.ai_rule: For a small operational scope, reversibility and clear responsibility, suggest V15.

decision_methods.name: Consensus
decision_methods.best_for: a small group whose joint action cannot practically work without broad agreement
decision_methods.avoid: large groups, time pressure, power imbalances or situations where silence is read as agreement
steps: Ask explicitly whether everyone can support it
decision_methods.example: A small shared household agrees on a common rule for their private home life.
decision_methods.risk: pressure to reach consensus, hidden vetoes, endless meetings
decision_methods.minority: Can strongly protect minorities, but also create an individual veto
decision_methods.legal: No substitute for a legally required majority
decision_methods.status: An experiment or process, not a universal obligation
decision_methods.ai_rule: Recommend only when genuinely joint implementation requires broad agreement and exit and protection are available.

decision_methods.name: Lottery / sortition
decision_methods.best_for: advisory or review councils, new perspectives and access to power without election campaigns
decision_methods.avoid: roles requiring specialist qualifications, permanent executive power or a manipulated pool
steps: Form a suitable pool of volunteers
decision_methods.example: A temporary mirror council is drawn by lot from a trained volunteer pool.
decision_methods.risk: pool bias, low participation, briefing/moderator capture
decision_methods.minority: Can include underrepresented perspectives; requires pool design
decision_methods.strategy: Manipulating the pool rather than the draw
decision_methods.legal: Does not replace statutory bodies or professional duties
decision_methods.status: D05 pilot and a strong review mechanism
decision_methods.ai_rule: For temporary advice or review and a recurring availability elite, consider V17.

decision_methods.name: Liquid Delegation
decision_methods.best_for: a large network with topic-specific self-selection and delegable expertise
decision_methods.avoid: a small group, lack of transparency or uncontrolled superdelegates
decision_methods.example: A member revocably delegates environmental questions to a trusted specialist.
decision_methods.strength: Flexible between direct and delegated participation
decision_methods.risk: Concentration of power, chains and technical dependency
decision_methods.minority: Can facilitate access but does not automatically protect minorities
decision_methods.legal: Experimental only; check the statutes and GenG
decision_methods.ai_rule: Suggest only in a large network, by topic, revocably and with visible concentration.

decision_methods.name: Quadratic Voting
decision_methods.best_for: express the intensity of several preferences with identical, limited credit allocations
decision_methods.avoid: the basic political vote, purchasable credits, essential rights or limited understanding of the method
steps: The cost of additional votes is quadratic
decision_methods.example: A community lab prioritises several experimental features.
decision_methods.risk: Complex, vulnerable to credit or identity manipulation, and close to currency
decision_methods.minority: An intense minority can gain weight, but equal resources are critical
decision_methods.legal: Core votes must never be purchasable; legal review
decision_methods.ai_rule: Only as a limited, non-purchasable pilot outside legally governed core politics.

decision_methods.name: Participatory budgeting
decision_methods.best_for: distribute a clearly bounded community budget through proposals, review and democratic selection
decision_methods.avoid: the entire core budget without reserves or legal review, or essential emergency aid
decision_methods.example: A community allocates a 10.000 € project budget to local initiatives.
decision_methods.strength: Combines ideas, learning and real resources
decision_methods.risk: Popular, visible projects dominate; implementation costs
decision_methods.minority: Separate windows for minorities or needs are possible
decision_methods.legal: Check budget, authority and procurement law
decision_methods.status: Suitable for a limited community budget
decision_methods.ai_rule: For a clearly limited voluntary project budget, recommend V20 plus suitable V06/V07/V14.

decision_methods.name: Dot voting / multi-dot polling
decision_methods.best_for: a quick, non-binding shortlist, agenda or topic cluster
decision_methods.avoid: a final decision on rights, staffing or money
steps: Treat the result as input only
decision_methods.example: A workshop marks which five questions should be explored further.
decision_methods.risk: Peer pressure, herding and false precision
decision_methods.minority: A minority can become visible but is easily outvoted
decision_methods.legal: Advisory only, without formal legal effect
decision_methods.ai_rule: Only as a preliminary filter or agenda, never as a hidden binding decision.

decision_methods.name: Drawing lots / random tie-break
decision_methods.best_for: a genuine tie between equivalent, reversible options, or a fair order
decision_methods.avoid: high stakes, fundamental rights, mandatory competence or unequal options
steps: Establish equivalence and a tie beforehand
Define the random procedure in advance
decision_methods.example: Two equally suitable teams allocate a pilot starting place by lot.
decision_methods.strength: Neutralises power struggles where there is genuine equivalence
decision_methods.risk: Chance can obscure responsibility
decision_methods.minority: Fair for equivalent opportunities, not for protection needs
decision_methods.strategy: Manipulation of the pool or draw
decision_methods.legal: Only where legally permitted
decision_methods.ai_rule: Suggest only when equivalence is genuinely justified and the decision is reversible.
